positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Implemented Tree Tracking API using Kotlin + Spring Boot. Fleshed out API details to include error handling and more complex edge cases. Learned Kotlin during this project.

Negotiated a significant refactor of our React/Typescript web application. Created a networking layer that handles API response errors, which fixed the issue where a single API failure would crash the app. Rearchitected data flow of the application to be unidirectional by replacing Recoil usage with more simple React useState hooks + props. Surfaced widespread lack of edge-case handling and fixed the most egregious issues. Fixed an infinite loop that was causing 106% CPU usage on an idle page.

Established code review process for the frontend team. Introduced Jest unit tests to our frontend in an effort to reduce reliance on slow and flaky Cypress tests. Introduced client side types for API responses to establish a separation of concern between the backend and frontend data models.

Mentor our frontend engineer on how to  build better abstractions and incorporate React best practices into their code. Code review changes for our senior backend engineer. Collaborate with Designers and Project Managers on new features.

Spearheaded recruiting efforts as interim hiring manager. Personally wrote recs for 2 of our 3 high priority engineering roles. Established our interview process. Led resume review, did recruiting screens & technical interviews. Hired one senior full stack engineer within the first 2 months.

positions.title: Instructor
positions.description:
Learned Javascript & React and began teaching introductory frontend programming within two months.

Led instruction for two 40-student cohorts at any given time. Met with students regularly to discuss progress. Held office hours to answer technical questions. Worked closely with Student Success to identify struggling students and help get them back on track.

Led monthly Unit Success Squad meetings where we reviewed metrics from recently graduated Unit 2 cohorts and made immediate improvements. Proposed larger-scale improvements at instruction-wide LEARN meetings.

Created class homepages to improve communication to students about o�ffice hours and support. 

Created pilot student tracking system that allows instructors to see a high level overview of a cohort's progress during any one sprint. That tracking system was absorbed into a larger student intervention process.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Designed, tested, and prototyped an async event bus that allows other teams to listen and respond to sharing-related events (Python).

Architected the server-side design for a new feature that allows users to sync data outside of their Dropbox folder. Presented several options for architecture review by senior and staff engineers. Negotiated for the client team to implement the backend, without further resources for my team, in a way that created the least complex interactions with code my team owned.

Managed agile process as team Scrum Master. Led 2x monthly retrospectives & daily stand up. Led task and project-level estimation exercises to clarify scope, blockers, and engineering cost.

honors.title: Gold Duke of Edinburgh Award (DOE)
honors.description:
Was awarded a Bronze, Silver, and Gold DOE Award. Each level involves a regular commitment to volunteering, physical activities, and developing skills. Additionally, each level requires an expedition (e.g. hiking, kayaking, sailing), and the Gold Award also involves a residential project. Achieving all three levels usually takes all four years of high school.

A specific Gold Award breakdown:
1. Volunteering - 12 months (Tutoring)
2. Physical activity- 12 months (Rugby)
3. Skills - 6 months (Thai Boxing)
4. Expedition- Plan, train for and undertake a 4 day, 3 night expedition (Sailing)
5. Undertake a shared activity in a residential setting away from home for 5 days and 4 nights.

More information can be found at: http://www.dofe.org/
honors.issuer: Issued by The Duke of Edinburgh Award · Jun 2014

honors.title: United States Presidential Scholar Candidate
honors.description:
"The U.S. Presidential Scholars Program was established in 1964, by executive order of the President, to recognize and honor some of our nation's most distinguished graduating high school seniors. In 1979, the program was extended to recognize students who demonstrate exceptional talent in the visual, creative and performing arts. Each year, up to 141 students are named as Presidential Scholars, one of the nation's highest honors for high school students."

--From the U.S. Department of Education's website, 
   http://www2.ed.gov/programs/psp/index.html
honors.issuer: Issued by U.S. Department of Education · Mar 2014
